verdicts.quote: When 1 place opens for an occurrence with an eligible active entry, the selected member gets a confirmed booking without having to claim or accept the place.
The earliest accepted active entry among eligible waiters receives the next place … close-together joins need a stable order without prescribing how to break a tie
verdicts.missing: The first eligible entry has priority, but the spec leaves the tie-breaker unspecified and does not say whether staff may override that order.

verdicts.quote: A member with a booking from the waitlist can cancel under the same conditions as a member with an otherwise equivalent ordinary booking.
verdicts.missing: The ordinary cancellation policy applies once promoted. The spec does not say whether missing the automatically booked class counts as a no-show.

verdicts.quote: If cancellation releases 1 place and a member is eligible on the waitlist, 1 waiting member gets a confirmed booking.
verdicts.missing: Cancellation triggers assignment without the waiter's participation, but the maximum delay from release to confirmation is unspecified.

verdicts.quote: Waitlist assignment can fill multiple newly bookable places … Concurrent actions cannot assign the same available place more than once … one waitlist entry yields at most 1 confirmed booking.
With 1 place bookable, concurrent actions that could consume it produce at most 1 new confirmed booking for the place.
verdicts.missing: The spec protects the seat but does not resolve a direct booking racing the same member's promotion, including how to reconcile their entry if the direct booking succeeds.

verdicts.quote: For a class and member population the app otherwise supports, an eligible member's join cannot be refused solely because of the number of entries already on the waitlist.
When the existing booking rules make it permanently too late to book an occurrence, members no longer see active entries for it.
verdicts.missing: The spec does not establish how far before class start promotions stop or whether the ordinary booking deadline falls before the start at all.

verdicts.quote: An increase that creates bookable places allows the waitlist to advance. A reduction does not cancel existing bookings through waitlist processing.
Canceling or removing an occurrence ends its active waitlist entries
When a member with an active entry joins again, the original entry continues to count from its original acceptance.
verdicts.missing: Active state and acceptance order are specified, but the builder must decide whether to record the join timestamp and whether to store or derive queue position.

verdicts.quote: When the existing booking rules make it permanently too late to book an occurrence, members no longer see active entries for it.
verdicts.missing: The spec ends active waiting at permanent closure but gives no retention period or deletion rule for ended entries.

verdicts.quote: A regular member checking their own waitlist status is not shown the identities of other waiters.
verdicts.missing: The spec does not say whether members can see their own numerical position.

verdicts.quote: Starting the updated app with a working existing booking configuration lets members join eligible full occurrences without an operator configuring the waitlist.
verdicts.missing: Default enablement is clear, but the spec does not define an off switch or controls for individual classes or class types.

verdicts.quote: If cancellation releases 1 place and a member is eligible on the waitlist, 1 waiting member gets a confirmed booking.
verdicts.missing: The builder has no upper bound on elapsed time between cancellation and promotion.

verdicts.quote: Ordinary booking continues through the existing flow when a place is available for ordinary booking … Existing confirmed bookings retain their status after the update
Existing full classes can accept waiters without being recreated.
